newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Annan says U.N. ready to work with new Zaire govt.
newsitem.headline: Annan says U.N. ready to work with new Zaire govt.

text.p: U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan said on Monday the United Nations was ready to work with a new government in Zaire and appealed to the international community to help the country on the road to recovery.
Annan, who is on a three-day visit to Vienna, said he was gratified that there had been no major bloodshed in Kinshasa as the forces of rebel leader Laurent Kabila took control of the capital.

"As you know the United Nations, ours is a big tent, and we work with all governments and we will work with the new government," Annan told reporters before meeting Austrian Defence Minister Werner Fasslabend. "I am gratified that there was no major bloodshed in Kinshasa."
Annan said he had spoken to his special envoy in Zaire Mohamed Sahnoun, who held talks with Kabila on Sunday.

The U.N. chief said he now hoped that Kabila would set to work on forming a broad-based government to include other political opposition movements apart from his Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo (AFDL).

"I appeal to the international community to work for the recovery of Zaire and I think if we handle it properly and work with the government that will be broad-based we can set Zaire on the road to national reconciliation, democracy and eventual prosperity because it is a very rich country," Annan said.
